Daily Brief

US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are heading to Kyiv on Sunday following three hours of talks with Vladimir Putin in Moscow, marking the first visit by Trump's top negotiators to Ukraine's capital as both sides agreed to a three-day pause on strikes against each other's capitals [BBC], [France 24], [RFI]. Meanwhile, the US-Iran conflict escalated sharply as both nations traded retaliatory attacks on ships in the Gulf, with the US 'permanently disabling' two Iranian oil tankers and Iran claiming strikes on US-affiliated vessels in response [BBC], [Globe and Mail]. In Germany, voters in Saxony-Anhalt head to polls where the far-right AfD is polling above 40 percent and could secure its first state-level power since World War II, a development being closely watched across Europe [BBC], [Le Monde], [RFI], [Financial Times]. The Anak Krakatau volcano eruption has stranded over 150,000 passengers after forcing the closure of six Indonesian airports including Jakarta's main international hub [BBC], [Globe and Mail]. Israeli air strikes killed four people in southern Lebanon despite an ongoing ceasefire, with Israel claiming the strikes responded to Hezbollah drone launches [France 24], [Al Jazeera].

01 Geopolitics

US Envoys Head to Kyiv After Three-Hour Kremlin Talks with Putin

  • Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held three hours of closed-door talks with Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin on Saturday, described by Russian officials as 'constructive and extremely frank'
  • Both Putin and Zelensky agreed to halt strikes on each other's capitals for three days during the negotiations
  • The envoys are expected to arrive in Kyiv on Sunday, marking their first visit to Ukraine's capital since Trump returned to office
  • Kremlin adviser Yuri Ushakov stated discussions covered economic issues and potential 'mutually beneficial Russian-American projects' beyond the Ukraine crisis

Germany's Far-Right AfD Poised for Historic State Election Victory in Saxony-Anhalt

  • AfD polling above 40 percent in Saxony-Anhalt, approximately 15-20 points ahead of Chancellor Merz's CDU
  • 35-year-old lead candidate Ulrich Siegmund could become AfD's first state premier if party wins outright majority
  • An absolute majority would mark the first time a far-right party has held state-level power in Germany's post-war era
  • The party has campaigned on tougher immigration rules, deportation of undocumented migrants, and closer ties with Russia

Anak Krakatau Eruption Strands 150,000 Passengers as Indonesia Closes Six Airports

  • Jakarta's Soekarno-Hatta International Airport and five other airports suspended operations due to volcanic ash reaching up to 50,000 feet
  • At least 467 flights affected including international routes to Singapore, Doha, Sydney and Kuala Lumpur
  • Volcano began erupting late Friday night with continuous seismic activity, lava fountains, and booming sounds; two more eruptions occurred early Sunday
  • Transport ministry urged airlines to expedite refunds and provide timely information to avoid airport overcrowding

Israeli Strikes Kill Four in Southern Lebanon Despite Ceasefire

  • Israeli air strikes on southern Lebanon killed four people including two women and wounded at least 20 others
  • Israel's military said strikes were response to Hezbollah launching two drones at Israeli soldiers in the self-declared 'security zone'
  • Strikes hit multiple locations including Nabatieh, Arab Salim, Nabatieh al-Fawqa and Kfar Reman
  • Lebanon's health ministry said the death toll was provisional; Israel issued its first 'evacuation' notice in Lebanon in several weeks
